Article Title: First exam reforms, now 'school thik karo' campaign: How CJP is changing the discourse of politics
Article Text:
School students protest in UP

'Ministers’ dogs got better facilities than students'

CJP claims credit

Politial parties take a cue from CJP

Youth outreach

NEW DELHI: From colleges to schools. From Gen Z to Gen Alpha. From Jantar Mantar to cities and villages in states. The students’ protest has continued; only the stage has shifted. The Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) “School Thik Karo” campaign has put the spotlight on the sorry condition of government schools in many states. Gen Z showed the way from Jantar Mantar when they forced the NDA government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign over NEET paper leaks. Gen Alpha took the cue and brought the protests to villages and towns across states, demanding better school infrastructure and government accountability.The CJP campaign asking for school audits in villages got a huge response. The pictures and videos of schools uploaded on CJP’s X timeline exposed the sorry state of government schools across states. This was followed by ground inspections by CJP teams, which led to confrontation and a strong pushback by some state governments.Two days after the CJP launched its campaign and announced that schools in Rajasthan would be on its radar, the state education department issued new guidelines regulating the entry of outsiders, including media personnel, into government schools.Under the directives, photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and live streaming involving students or school activities on campus needed prior permission from the school principal or head of the institution.The Rajasthan order went on to threaten action under applicable laws in case of any breach.So, when a CJP team went to inspect a government school on August 21, it was attacked and forcibly pushed back, allegedly by the locals. Videos of the incident showed a large number of people engaging in a heated exchange with the CJP team, pushing and shoving its members as they tried to enter the village. Some clips also showed stone-pelting and smashed windows of cars. Locals said the village did not need outside political groups to intervene in the school’s affairs.This perhaps became the July 20 Jantar Mantar moment (when Delhi Police used force to stop Gen Z protesters from their Sansad march) of the CJP school campaign as the violent confrontation propelled the issue to the national centre stage.Meanwhile in Uttar Pradesh, Gen Alpha students of a government school staged a protest twice, in a span of four days. over shortage of subject teachers. They briefly blocked traffic also. Students of a government school in Kannauj boycotted classes and held protests against the principal for alleged caste discrimination and ordering the felling of trees inside the school campus. The students of PM Shri Composite School in Gugarapur surrounded the vehicle of the in-charge principal at the school gate as he was leaving and raised slogans against him.Protests also happened in Fatehpur, Hamirpur against lack of facilities in schools. In Hamirpur, 'Gen Alpha' children laid siege to the collectorate to demand the construction of a paved road to their school.In Unnao, hundreds of students of a government-run residential school staged a protest over alleged poor-quality food, inadequate drinking water, shortage of teachers and the behaviour of the principal, briefly disrupting traffic at a city crossing.In Maharashtra, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke conducted a social audit of government-run and municipal schools in Latur district. He led a team at a Zilla Parishad school at Ujani village in Latur's Ausa tehsil.After his audit, Dipke said schools in the state were in a pitiable condition, and even "ministers’ dogs got better facilities" than students. He sought the resignation of Maharashtra school education minister Dada Bhuse. Later, Maharashtra police registered a case against the CJP convenor and others for allegedly entering a government school without permission, disrupting official work and threatening teachers.The state governments cited rules to browbeat the CJP teams away from its schools. But at the same time, they were forced to act to nullify the impact of the CJP campaign. So, while some states announced new measures to improve the condition of schools, others increased the pace of work already underway to ensure that results were seen on the ground quickly.The CJP was quick to claim credit for govt actions and basked in glory.“The impact we’ve been able to make with such a small team in such a short span of time is just unreal. Multiple state governments have had to bow down. Authorities had to listen to Gen Z and Gen Alpha kids and give them their due,” it said in a post on X.“But this does not end here. We need to keep going until even the remotest regions of the nation, even the most deprived communities, have access to the highest standard of educational facilities. They may use force, they may file cases, they may do whatever they can to crush this, but we will remain committed to the same demand,” the post read.While it can be debated whether or not the CJP campaign forced the governments into action, what can be said with certainty is that the CJP has managed to do what many political parties could not - inspire the youth to come to the streets and seek accountability from power.The two CJP campaigns also point to an interesting shift - which should be a learning lesson, especially for parties in the opposition space. We have seen the opposition parties raise the pitch against government on issues like caste and religion as these have greater potential for voter mobilisation. Rarely do we see campaigns by the opposition parties centred around health or education reforms. But that seems to have changed.The Congress has taken a cue and is trying to stay focused on students’ connect and raise issues that concern the youth. In Rajasthan, the state Congress unit is also on the streets to highlight gaps in state government school infrastructure.And it’s not just the opposition that is course-correcting; the ruling BJP has also drawn a roadmap to engage with the youth and understand their concerns. In the middle of the Gen Z protest, Prime Minister Narendra Modi debuted on Instagram and tried to communicate directly with the youth who were on the streets. The BJP has in fact formed a dedicated team to spearhead its Gen Z outreach. The team includes BJP chief Nitin Nabin, national general secretaries Smriti Irani and Vinod Tawde, Gujarat minister Harsh Sanghavi, Chhattisgarh minister OP Choudhary, along with several other leaders.Clearly, the CJP has managed to change the political discourse and has put the focus on the youth as potential game-changers in electoral politics. As we gear up for the next rounds of assembly elections in the run-up to the 2029 Lok Sabha challenge, we may see youth outreach taking centre stage like never before.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) “School Thik Karo’ campaign has put the spotlight on the sorry condition of government schools in many states. The CJP campaign asking for school audits in villages got a huge response. This was followed by ground inspections by CJP teams, which led to confrontation and a strong pushback by state governments.

Article Title: 'BJP thinks it is bigger than RSS, it should listen to Mohan Bhagwat': CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke
Article Text:
Dipke says BJP should at least listen to Mohan Bhagwat who is their mentor.

What Bhagwat said in New York

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday urged the BJP to “listen to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat”, accusing the ruling party of believing that it had grown bigger than the organisation.Dipke's remarks came after Bhagwat, while addressing an event in New York, said that a Hindu who believes Muslims should not live in Bharat cannot be considered a Hindu.Dipke also criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his reported use of the term “Dimagi Naxal” for protesting Gen Z.“I have been saying this from the beginning that the BJP should listen to Mohan Bhagwat . After being in power for 12 years and having so many agencies in its hands, BJP is thinking that it has grown bigger than the RSS,” Dipke said.He said Bhagwat had earlier cautioned against calling protesting Gen Z youths “anti-national”, but Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the term “Dimagi Naxal”.“But the PM (Narendra Modi) came up with a new word, 'Dimagi Naxal'. It clearly shows that the PM is not listening to Mohan Bhagwat,” Dipke said.He added that while the RSS chief speaks about inclusivity and respecting children, the use of such terms by the prime minister “doesn't look good”.“They should at least listen to Mohan Bhagwat who is their mentor... they (BJP) are in power because of the RSS,” Dipke said.Dipke also rejected suggestions that activist Sonam Wangchuk 's comments about CJP leaders indicated that they had political ambitions. Responding to a question about Wangchuk's interview with a YouTube channel, Dipke said the activist's remarks had been distorted.“He was asked whether Sourav (Das) and Ashutosh (Ranka) are having any ambitions. Wangchuk said that we are talented and good leaders and have not been corrupt till now. We have run the agitation honestly,” Dipke said. “He has spoken good things about us,” he added.Addressing the ‘One World One Humanity’ event in New York, Bhagwat said different religions may follow different paths, but humanity and truth remain one.“We come from a society that believes humanity is one. If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslims in India, then he's not a Hindu….” the RSS chief said.“If you want call yourself hindu than you must believe that all paths are leading to the same. And every human has a dignity. There is no difference between human beings,” he added.Bhagwat also stressed the need to protect diversity while maintaining unity. “I am not a religious scholar, nor a religious authority like you, but I am working in a society which traditionally says that religions might be different, but humanity is one.Truth is one, and humanity is a product of that truth. So humanity is one,” Bhagwat said.“That truth is one truth, but it is described in many ways according to the describer. Because as human beings, we are prisoners of the software that has been created in our heads,” he added.The event was organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD) and was described as a “landmark Raksha Bandhan gathering”.The programme focused on the theme of universal oneness and the Hindu philosophy of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’, or the world is one family.
Article Summary: CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke says BJP should at least listen to Mohan Bhagwat who is their mentor. Dipke also criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his reported use of the term “Dimagi Naxal” for protesting Gen Z.

Article Title: 'Oldest trick in RSS playbook': Owaisi attacks Mohan Bhagwat over Hindu-Muslim remarks
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Sunday criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity, alleging that the RSS projects a different image of itself to the world while the writings of its key thinkers reflect a different view of minorities.Owaisi's remarks came a day after Bhagwat, speaking at at event in New York, said that a Hindu who believes Muslims should not live in India would not remain a Hindu.Reacting to the remarks, Owaisi said, “This is the oldest trick in the RSS playbook: some words are for the world, and some are for its own members. The RSS has never disavowed its key thinkers and writers. What do they say about Muslims and other minorities?”Owaisi referred to a biography of RSS founder K B Hedgewar, published by the RSS, to claim that Hedgewar had opposed the Congress's emphasis on Hindu-Muslim unity.Quoting from the biography, Owaisi said, “Gandhiji worked constantly with one eye on Hindu-Muslim unity... But Doctorji sensed danger in that move. In fact, he did not even relish the newfangled slogan of 'Hindu-Muslim Unity'.”The AIMIM chief also cited former RSS chief M S Golwalkar's writings, referring to his book Bunch of Thoughts and its chapter titled 'Internal Threats'.“Golwalkar's 'Bunch of Thoughts' has a long chapter titled 'Internal Threats', in which Muslim and Christian citizens of India are described as threats number one and two, respectively,” Owaisi said.He also referred to Golwalkar's statement that the Sangh was “inspired by one flag (saffron), one leader and one ideology”.Owaisi alleged that the RSS did not contribute to India's freedom struggle and claimed that Hedgewar left the Congress because he opposed the participation of different religious communities in the anti-British movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.Owaisi also invoked the 2002 Gujarat riots while criticising the RSS, asking, “Should we forget what happened to the Muslims of Gujarat under the RSS's proxy rule?”He alleged that Muslims and Christians continued to face discrimination and claimed that Muslims were being subjected to Hindu law in the name of the Uniform Civil Code, while Christians were being targeted through “draconian” anti-conversion laws.The AIMIM chief also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).Earlier on Saturday, addressing the ‘One World One Humanity’ event in New York, Bhagwat said different religions may follow different paths, but humanity and truth remain one. “We come from a society that believes humanity is one,” he said.“If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu. If you want to call yourself Hindu, you must believe that all paths are leading to the same goal and that every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings,” Bhagwat had added.Bhagwat also used the occasion to speak about perceptions of the RSS. He said the organisation was often viewed through narratives that, in his view, did not reflect its work on the ground."There are many perceptions created by wrong narratives. But when you come and see us from inside, all those will be disbelieved in the day."The RSS chief was speaking in New York as he began a three-nation global outreach tour covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. The visit has been organised as part of the organisation's centenary year celebrations, following invitations from overseas local organisations.
Article Summary: AIMIM president criticises RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity. Owaisi says the RSS projects a different image of itself to the world. He says the writings of its key thinkers reflect a different view of minorities.

Article Title: 'We never thought they were Muslims': Mohan Bhagwat recalls 1996 Charkhi Dadri mid-air collision
Article Text:
RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat addresses at 'One World One Humanity' event, in New York on Saturday. (One World One Humanity/ ANI Video Grab)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Nearly three decades after one of the world’s deadliest aviation disasters, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat returned to the memory of the Charkhi Dadri mid-air collision in Haryana.He recalled the chaos that followed the crash. He spoke of injured passengers, bodies that had to be recovered and families arriving from far away, searching for their loved ones and trying to identify those they had lost. And he remembered the RSS volunteers who, according to him, reached the site and began helping.They treated the injured. They helped recover the dead. They assisted relatives who arrived later. They also helped arrange funeral rites.Many of the victims were Muslims. But Bhagwat said that was never a consideration for the volunteers who were serving them.Speaking at the "One World One Humanity" event in New York on Saturday, Bhagwat recalled the tragedy as an example of what he described as the RSS's philosophy of unconditional humanitarian service."Two planes collided over Haryana, which is part of Bharat, over the place named Dadri. Both were from Arab countries. Most of the passengers were Muslims. After that collision, our Swayamsevaks reached there first, and they served. Served in treating the injured... Recovering their bodies, arranging for the funeral rites when their relatives come, helping them in identifying. We never thought at that time that these were Muslims," said the RSS Chief.The disaster took place on November 12, 1996. A Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakhstan Airlines Ilyushin Il-76 collided in the skies over Charkhi Dadri, Haryana.There were no survivors.All 349 people aboard the two aircraft were killed. The crash became the deadliest mid-air collision in aviation history.For Bhagwat, the tragedy was not only about the terrible loss of life. It was also about what happened after the aircraft came down.He recalled a moment when grief and devastation had stripped away every distinction between people. Those at the crash site needed help. Families needed answers. The dead needed dignity.Bhagwat said the volunteers did not ask who the victims were before helping them.He also said the RSS did not publicise such work because it did not expect anything in return."The prominent working organisation was RSS. We could do this because we are not in politics. And we don't go on making these things famous because we don't want anything from this. No return... In Sangha, we only give. We don't want anything. That is why in publicity matters, we are way behind."The RSS chief was speaking in New York as he began a three-nation global outreach tour covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. The visit has been organised as part of the organisation's centenary year celebrations, following invitations from overseas local organisations.Bhagwat also used the occasion to speak about perceptions of the RSS. He said the organisation was often viewed through narratives that, in his view, did not reflect its work on the ground."There are many perceptions created by wrong narratives. But when you come and see us from inside, all those will be disbelieved in the day."He then broadened his argument beyond the RSS and its work during disasters. He spoke about the kind of social change he believes is necessary to create greater unity.Bhagwat said political systems alone could not bring about such change. In a democracy, he argued, political leaders ultimately respond to public opinion. The first step, therefore, had to be taken within society itself."Politics today, especially in a democracy, depends on the public view. If there is public opinion, then no politician will dare to go against it. Therefore, I think after taking a common resolve today, we have to act in these societies, and we have to act first locally."He argued that social harmony could not be built simply by gaining political power. It had to grow from everyday interactions and acts of service.For Bhagwat, the idea was rooted in what he described as the traditional thought of Bharat, where the unity of humanity is placed above individual interests."This is the traditional thought of Bharat--unity of humanity. All our leaders, at any point in time, have emphasised that too. After independence, we got the constitution, which emphasises this, but that is not happening. Because these things do not happen through politics. I'm sorry to say, but the fact is, politics has now become a game of self-interest. And where there is me and I, there is no solution. We and ours are the solution. So our experience in Bharat is that we have to start with society."He called for such efforts to begin locally. Small pockets of people working together, he said, could eventually become larger networks of service and unity."Whatever we decide to do today, we should start in our own country and create pockets of such selfless service, such an atmosphere of unity, and then this dialogue should continue. Through this dialogue, we should connect them, and then we should grow."Nearly 30 years after the Charkhi Dadri crash, the scale of the disaster remains difficult to comprehend. Hundreds of lives were lost in a matter of moments.But Bhagwat chose to remember what happened in the aftermath.Amid the wreckage, he said, volunteers came forward to help people they did not know. They treated the injured. They recovered bodies. They helped families search for answers.And, in his telling of that day, they did so without first asking whether the person in front of them was Hindu or Muslim.That memory formed the emotional centre of Bhagwat's message in New York: that in moments of profound human suffering, service can begin before identity does.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat spoke at the "One World One Humanity" event in New York. He recalled the Charkhi Dadri mid-air collision in Haryana in 1996. He said the tragedy was an example of what he described as RSS's philosophy of unconditional humanitarian service.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in a yoga session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan in Tashkent on Sunday, during his two-day state visit to Uzbekistan.PM Modi walked around the venue and interacted with participants as the group performed yoga. He also posed for a group photograph with the participants at the end of the session.The yoga programme came a day after PM Modi received a warm welcome from Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev following his arrival in Tashkent. They came back with great memories of India and the Championship. I commend the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan for their work towards making Yoga popular."The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Mirziyoyev later on Sunday, with discussions expected to focus on trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people ties.The visit is PM Modi’s fourth to Uzbekistan since becoming prime minister, following trips in 2015, 2016 and 2022. Article Title: 'RSS vision is to see the world as one': Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat at New York event
Article Text:
'Unity in diversity in Bharat's DNA: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat

‘Be true to America’: RSS chief message to diaspora

Highlights responsibility towards others

Bhagwat offers interpretation of Dharma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat , addressing around 5,000 members of Indian-American organisations at Madison Square Garden in New York, spoke about unity, pluralism, individual responsibility and the obligations of the Indian diaspora, while arguing that material success alone cannot define a fulfilling life.Bhagwat was speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration”, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue. He framed his address around the idea of “oneness”, drawing parallels between the pluralism associated with the United States and what he described as Bharat’s “unity in diversity”.“When we say America, United States of America, one word is often discussed frequently. That is pluralism,” Bhagwat said. “And when we say Bharat, another word, another phrase is discussed: unity in diversity.”“For Bharat, this unity and diversity, both are in their DNA,” he said.Bhagwat said differences between people were a natural feature of life, but argued that these differences existed alongside an underlying sense of oneness.“So many styles of living. We appear different. We are different,” he said, pointing to differences in people's everyday needs and circumstances.“But there is innate oneness. That is why we feel for each other,” he added.He described diversity as the “decoration of oneness”, presenting unity not as the absence of differences but as something that exists beneath them.Bhagwat also linked this idea to what he described as the responsibilities of individuals, societies and nations. Nations, he said, should not be seen merely as geographical entities but as having a larger purpose.“These nations are not merely geographical entities. In the design of this universe, nations have to carry out a duty,” he said, quoting Swami Vivekananda's formulation that every nation has a message, a mission and a destiny.Turning to the Indian diaspora in the United States, Bhagwat said Indians living abroad had a primary responsibility towards the country where they lived and worked.“So we are Americans, and we should be true to America,” he said.He described this as a duty towards one's “karma bhumi” — the land where a person lives and works.“The diaspora, Indian diaspora, they have a duty to their karma bhumi. They must fulfill that. They should be loyal to their karma bhumi,” Bhagwat said.At the same time, he said Indians abroad could maintain a connection with Bharat as their “janma bhumi”, or birthplace, and could contribute to the country if they wished to do so after fulfilling their responsibilities to their adopted home.“But it is not obligatory,” he said.Instead, he said, the connection with Bharat should be reflected in the values carried by the diaspora.“Your janma bhumi expects you to live the values it has imparted on you,” Bhagwat said.Bhagwat also questioned the idea that professional success should be measured primarily through earnings and material possessions.“How much we earn is not important. How much we distribute is important,” he said.He asked whether a career could be reduced to money and material happiness, while acknowledging that material aspirations had a legitimate place in Hindu philosophy.“You think of career? Is career only money? Is career only material happiness?” Bhagwat asked.He referred to the four Purusharthas, saying that Artha and Kama represented important material dimensions of life alongside spiritual pursuits.“It is not denied. In four Purusharthas, Artha and Kama are two important Purusharthas related to material life,” he said.Bhagwat also referred to the traditional four stages of life — Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa — arguing that people acquire different responsibilities as they move through life.“So you have to learn, you have to sustain life, and you have to give the advice, your experience to next generation,” he said.He argued that material abundance by itself could not guarantee fulfilment.“So the material happiness is transient, cannot satisfy,” Bhagwat said. “And if abundance of material happiness is there, it may fail also. And therefore there is no satisfaction.”Bhagwat's broader argument centred on the idea that human intelligence carried with it a responsibility towards others.Using the example of a hungry person watching someone eat, he said people instinctively recognise another person's suffering and cannot simply ignore it.“A simple experiment you can do, or I can challenge you to do. When you are taking your lunch or dinner, let a hungry man stand before you, and let him stare at your full platter with hungry eyes,” he said.“You can try; you will not do. Because we are human beings.”He contrasted human beings' ability to think and plan with the instinctive behaviour of animals, but said the ability to think also brought a responsibility to use that capacity correctly.“If you think in the right way, you go nearer to God. If you think in the wrong way, you go nearer to the animal kingdom,” he said.Bhagwat also offered a broader interpretation of “Dharma”, saying it should not be understood simply as religion or worship.“Dharma is not religion. It is not worship. It is beyond all this,” he said.He described Dharma as a sustaining principle that allows people and society to manage competing aspects of life and maintain balance.“It is the balance which sustains everything at once, simultaneously, and simultaneously everyone can progress,” Bhagwat said.He similarly argued that progress should not require either individuals or society to be suppressed.“Individual, society and environment, they have to proceed together, progress together,” he said, adding that different aspects of an individual's own life — body, mind and intellect — also had to advance together.Bhagwat concluded by returning to the idea of responsibility towards both one's place of work and birthplace.He called on people to fulfil their duties towards their “karma bhumi” as well as their “janma bhumi”, saying such an approach could help a world struggling with multiple challenges.“To that destiny and fulfill our duties in our karma bhumi as well as our janma bhumi,” he said.“If we do that, that will be a boon for the world struggling with all these problems and stumbling at every step.”
Article Summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke about unity, pluralism, individual responsibility and the obligations of the Indian diaspora. He was speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration’, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue.

Article Title: BJP-SAD alliance revival gains ground ahead of Punjab polls
Article Text:
Those in favour of the alliance have drawn strength fromModi’s meeting with Badal, on Aug 7, and the subsequent talks between the two parties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are likely to revive their alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly polls, with both parties acknowledging that it could be their best bet despite differences, especially over seat sharing.Since PM Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal on Aug 7, sources said both parties have engaged in talks. BJP will take the final call and has given no public hint about an alliance. Some Punjab functionaries said both parties had shown more pragmatism than in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, when their inflexibility derailed talks. Sources said ironing out the details of the alliance would prove more difficult than reaching an agreement on the alliance itself.Akali Dal is expected to remain the senior partner, but BJP is seeking a major increase in its seat share from the 2017 assembly polls, besides a bigger role in any future govt. BJP's vote share has risen since it began fighting elections alone, helped by the induction of several regional leaders from different parties. It crossed 18.5% in 2024, against nearly 13.5% for SAD.SAD and BJP fought 94 and 23 seats, respectively, when they contested the 2017 polls together. There is wide acknowledgement that the old equation no longer holds after a string of setbacks for SAD. The key question is how the two parties define the new alliance.
Article Summary: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are likely to revive their alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly polls. Both parties acknowledge that it could be their best bet despite differences, especially over seat sharing. Since PM Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal on Aug 7, sources said both parties have engaged in talks.

Article Title: Meet Marcus Klepacki, the 19-year-old Phoenix musician who learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm and is now debuting his own band
Article Text:
19-year-old Marcus Klepacki learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm

Early health battles and musical training

Formation of Third Man Factor

Stage debut at Yucca Tap Room

Nineteen-year-old Phoenix musician Marcus Klepacki is preparing for his first official public performance with his new rock band, Third Man Factor, at Tempe’s historic Yucca Tap Room. What makes the performance unusual is not only the venue but also the way Klepacki plays. Born without a right arm and without a thumb on his left hand, the 19-year-old plays a standard acoustic drum kit without any major changes, using only one arm. According to reports from the Phoenix New Times and coverage published by Hoodline, Klepacki finds comparisons with Def Leppard drummer Rick Allen amusing, but says their approaches are very different. Allen lost his left arm in a 1984 car crash and later used a specially designed electronic drum system with foot pedals. Klepacki, however, plays entirely on acoustic drums, relying on physical skill and his own playing technique. "I think people need to know that Marcus, he's not good for having one arm; he's just good," Chuck Savale, a music instructor who coached Klepacki, told the Phoenix New Times.Klepacki’s journey to the stage has followed years of serious health problems.He was diagnosed with scoliosis at age 3 and wore a corrective back brace from kindergarten until he entered high school. At age 7, he was diagnosed with leukaemia and underwent three and a half years of chemotherapy. In 2021, Dr Greg White, head of paediatric spinal surgery at Phoenix Children’s Hospital, performed surgery to correct Klepacki’s spine. White also plays bass in local cover band Central Line. In 2024, he invited Klepacki’s former music group to open for his band at Copper Blues Live in Desert Ridge. Throughout his medical challenges, his parents, Alex and Melissa Klepacki, made sure he could take part in normal childhood activities. His formal music education began at around age 10 when he started lessons at Alice Cooper’s Solid Rock Teen Centers, a Phoenix non-profit that provides free arts training to young people. Reports by the Phoenix New Times explain how Savale taught Klepacki by practising with only one arm himself. This helped him understand techniques that could produce a full and strong sound. Within a few years, Klepacki had learned difficult drumming patterns, including the famous "Purdie shuffle" created by legendary session drummer Bernard Purdie. The rhythm uses a half-time beat with triplet hi-hat patterns and soft snare notes. "It blew my mind when I saw Marcus do that," Savale told reporters, adding that the young drummer quickly moved beyond his own technical abilities.Klepacki gained more performance experience by joining marching and concert bands at Shadow Mountain High School in Phoenix. He also played drums at around half a dozen showcases for Alice Cooper charity events. Third Man Factor’s lineup came together mainly through Arizona State University’s Bachelor of Arts in Popular Music programme at the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts. Alongside Klepacki on drums are lead vocalist Fletcher Placko, guitarists Chris Sanchez and Ben Pakula, and bassist Noah Paz. Speaking to the Phoenix New Times, Placko praised Klepacki’s team spirit and natural ability. He said the other musicians quickly respected his talent when they played together during university classes. The band takes inspiration from 1990s alternative rock and grunge. Klepacki’s own drumming influences include Rush’s Neil Peart, Led Zeppelin’s John Bonham, The Police’s Stewart Copeland, Buddy Rich and The White Stripes’ Meg White.The chance to perform at Yucca Tap Room came after the mother of the frontman of local band The Black Hole saw Klepacki play at an open-mic event at the Solid Rock Teen Center. She later offered him a place on the bill, according to Hoodline and Phoenix New Times reports. Open since the 1960s, Yucca Tap Room is Tempe’s oldest active live music venue. Over the years, it has helped launch and support independent rock and punk bands from across the East Valley. The Sunday afternoon show features Third Man Factor alongside a six-band lineup. The bill includes headliners The Black Hole, Band of Fools, the Hard Bop Group, Just About Halfway and Rino. Looking ahead, Klepacki hopes to build a long-term career in music. He is considering work as a touring performer, session musician or record producer. Reflecting on his experiences and future, Klepacki told the Phoenix New Times: "Part of my attitude is: I went through some of the hardest things people could go through early on."
Article Summary: Marcus Klepacki was born without a right arm and without a thumb on his left hand. The 19-year-old learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm. His new band, Third Man Factor, will perform at Tempe's Yucca Tap Room.

Article Title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
Article Text:
Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family

What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?

How did becoming a father change Agassi’s view of his own childhood?

How did Steffi Graf fit into Agassi’s approach to raising their children?

What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Andre Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Andre Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Tennis legend Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf have two children, Jaden and Jaz. Agassi’s famous quote, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children's childhood,” offers a look at how becoming a parent changed his view of his own life. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood.

Article Title: He died at 23 after fighting in the Korean War; nearly 74 years later Willie Estrada’s family is still pushing for him to receive the Medal of Honor
Article Text:
Mario Estrada (left) and Pete Estrada (right) vow to continue the effort to win the Medal of Honor for war hero Willie Estrada (pictured).

Carlsbad Current-Argus

Last stand at Hill 223

Legacy and decorations in New Mexico

The legal path to an award upgrade

The process usually involves:

Congressional sponsorship: A member of Congress must introduce special waiver legislation to get around the normal time limits set under Title 10 of the United States Code.

A member of Congress must introduce special waiver legislation to get around the normal time limits set under Title 10 of the United States Code. Service branch review: The Senior Army Board for Correction of Military Records examines battle reports, statements from surviving crew members and recommendations from commanders.

The Senior Army Board for Correction of Military Records examines battle reports, statements from surviving crew members and recommendations from commanders. Department approval: The Secretary of the Army and Secretary of Defense must formally support the upgraded award.

The Secretary of the Army and Secretary of Defense must formally support the upgraded award. Presidential authorisation: The Medal of Honor is ultimately presented by the President of the United States on behalf of Congress.

Nearly 74 years after Sergeant Willie Noriega Estrada died while protecting his tank crew during the Korean War, his family is still working to have his military award upgraded to the Medal of Honor. The New Mexico native was 23 when he was killed in action on 22 September 1952 near Bongowol, North Korea. He became the first draftee from Otero County to receive the Distinguished Service Cross, the US Army’s second-highest award for extraordinary heroism. According to reporting by the, his brothers Mario Estrada and Pete Estrada remain determined to make sure his actions receive the country’s highest military honour.In September 1952, Sergeant Estrada was a tank commander with Company C of the 245th Medium Tank Battalion, attached to the 45th Infantry Division. During a fierce overnight battle involving an estimated 2,000 enemy troops, his unit came under heavy artillery and anti-tank fire. Military records and historical accounts preserved by Honor States describe how Estrada’s tank crew fought enemy forces for 15 hours to protect nearby infantry positions.As enemy bazooka rounds began hitting and penetrating the tanks, Estrada ordered a second tank nearby to pull back to safety while he stayed behind to cover its retreat. Estrada suffered terrible injuries, including losing an arm after a shaped-charge round pierced his tank turret. Despite his wounds, he continued firing his machine gun to slow the advancing enemy forces. When friendly troops reached the hill the next morning, they found Estrada alive inside the damaged tank. He died from severe blood loss shortly after rescue teams arrived. Soldiers approaching the position also found Chinese graffiti written on the tank’s steel hull that read "Brave Fighter". It had been left by enemy troops who had passed the position.Estrada remains the most decorated military service member in Otero County’s history. In addition to the Distinguished Service Cross, his awards include the Silver Star with Oak Leaf Cluster, the Purple Heart, the Air Medal with Oak Leaf Cluster and the Republic of Korea Presidential Unit Citation. His hometown of Alamogordo honoured him on 3 June 2004 by naming its municipal facility the Willie Estrada Memorial Civic Center. His name has also been given to military sites outside New Mexico, including a street at Fort Knox, Kentucky, and an Army training camp in South Korea. Despite these honours, his family believes his actions deserve the Medal of Honor. Because many decades have passed since the war, securing an upgrade requires congressional action or presidential approval.Upgrading a military award for bravery many decades after a war involves a detailed review by the US Department of Defense and Congress. Under federal military rules, requests to upgrade awards must provide new and previously unavailable historical evidence or show that an administrative error stopped the original recommendation from being properly considered.Mario and Pete Estrada continue to collect military records and work with veterans’ advocacy groups as they seek support from lawmakers for a formal congressional review. The family says its campaign is not about adding another decoration, but about completing the official record of a soldier who gave his life to protect his fellow crew members on a remote Korean ridge.
Article Summary: Estrada was the first member of his family to be awarded the Medal of Honor. He was shot in the back of the head by an enemy tank during the Korean War. He died on September 22, 1950. His family is now trying to get the award upgraded to the highest honour.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, breaks all-time Duleep Trophy record in semi-final

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has added another record to his rapidly growing list of achievements, becoming the youngest batter in Duleep Trophy history to score a half-century.The 15-year-old achieved the feat during East Zone’s Duleep Trophy 2026 semi-final against Central Zone in Bengaluru, reaching his fifty in just 42 balls with a six.Sooryavanshi eventually finished with an impressive 92 off 81 balls, falling just eight runs short of a century. His knock included aggressive strokeplay and came at a crucial stage for East Zone.At 15 years and 175 days, Sooryavanshi surpassed a record that had stood for 57 years. The previous youngest batter to score a Duleep Trophy fifty was Laxman Singh, who was 16 years and 23 days old when he achieved the feat in 1969.He has now moved ahead of Laxman Singh and Piyush Chawla, who was 16 years and 307 days old when he scored a Duleep Trophy fifty in 2025.Sooryavanshi’s batting milestone came after he had already found himself in an unusual leadership role earlier in the match.On Day 1, East Zone captain Ishan Kishan was forced off the field during the morning session after being struck on his right wrist. Sooryavanshi stepped in as stand-in captain for around an hour on either side of lunch before Kishan returned to take charge.During his brief spell as captain, Sooryavanshi also made an important intervention with the DRS.In the 40th over, Central Zone opener and wicketkeeper Aryan Juyal was on 46 when he poked at a delivery from Mukesh Kumar outside off. East Zone appealed for a caught-behind dismissal, but the on-field umpire turned it down.Sooryavanshi backed his judgement and opted for a review. UltraEdge showed a small spike as the ball passed the bat, confirming the edge and giving East Zone a crucial wicket.Earlier, East Zone made an excellent start after Kishan won the toss and chose to field.Mukesh Kumar and Abhijit Sarkar picked up three wickets apiece, while Mohammed Shami and off-spinner Md Kounain Quraishi claimed two each as Central Zone were bowled out for 266 in 80.1 overs.Rinku Singh top-scored with 60 off 88 balls, while Juyal contributed 46. Rinku also put together a 55-run sixth-wicket partnership with Harsh Dubey, who scored 27, after Central Zone slipped to 125/5.Quraishi broke that stand by trapping Dubey lbw in the 60th over, triggering another collapse. Saransh Jain made 13 and Aryan Pandey scored 22, while Yash Thakur provided late impetus with a quick 30 off 26 balls.Central Zone were eventually bowled out for 266, giving East Zone the platform to take control of the semi-final.For Sooryavanshi, the semi-final has already been a memorable one. On the opening day, he briefly took over as East Zone captain after Ishan Kishan left the field, and a day later he produced another record-breaking performance. Sooryavanshi brought up his half-century in just 42 balls before going on to score 92 off 81 deliveries.The only disappointment was that the teenage star could not complete another century, falling just eight runs short of three figures.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the youngest batter in Duleep Trophy history to score a half-century. The 15-year-old achieved the feat during East Zone’s semi-final against Central Zone in Bengaluru. He reached his fifty in just 42 balls with a six, before going on to score 92 off 81 deliveries. At 15 years and 175 days, he surpassed a record that had stood for 57 years. He has now moved ahead of Laxman Singh and Piyush Chawla.

Article Title: Players at the US Open in New York are complaining that the smell of marijuana is becoming an unwanted distraction
Article Text:
Players at the US Open in New York say marijuana smoke is becoming an unexpected distraction/ Photo by Dave Dellinger/USTA

Boulter: ‘You don't need distractions’

Jones remembers the smell from last year's US Open

It has been an issue at the US Open before

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 2026 US Open is set to begin on Sunday, but as the world's best players prepare for the year's final Grand Slam, some competitors are dealing with an unexpected distraction around Flushing Meadows: the smell of cannabis drifting in from a nearby park.British players Katie Boulter, Fran Jones and Harriet Dart have all noticed the smell around the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, with Boulter saying it can affect her concentration during practice and matches.The tournament begins on Aug. 30, with Carlos Alcaraz returning to individual competition for the first time since suffering a wrist injury at the Barcelona Open in April. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner will miss the event with a knee injury, while Novak Djokovic will pursue a record 25th Grand Slam title. Rising star Alex Eala is also expected to receive strong support from New York fans, while Aryna Sabalenka will look to rediscover her best form.Cannabis is legal for adults aged 21 and over in New York, although smoking is not permitted on the grounds of the tennis center. However, the venue sits beside Corona Park, and the smell can carry across to some practice and outside courts.Boulter, Britain's No. 1 and ranked 60th in the world, said she has encountered it both while practising and during matches.“Yeah, I have experienced it. You go down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot,” Boulter said.“But yeah, I'm not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on some of the specific courts.“I've played on one before and I did smell it during my match. It's something that I wouldn't like to smell in the middle of my match.“I'm trying to focus and then obviously, it takes you out of the moment and you really don't want to. You don't need distractions. So yeah, I wasn't a huge fan of it.”Boulter is not the only British player to have noticed it. Fran Jones, Britain's No. 3, recalled encountering the smell during her first-round match at last year's tournament and said she initially wondered whether it was simply part of playing so close to the park.“Last year I made a joke about that, in my first round, and I said to the guy, 'is this normal?' Because I was on the stadium, and it's next to the park,” Jones said.“He's like, 'yeah.' and I was like, 'well, no wonder I'm playing pretty well.'“This year I'll be like 'no, lock in, lock in!'”Jones, who qualified for this year's tournament, begins her campaign against Poland's Magda Linette on Monday.Harriet Dart, who also came through qualifying, took a more typically New York approach to the situation.“I mean it's New York. It's New York. I feel like everywhere you walk around, it's everywhere, no? It is what it is. Same for everyone,” Dart said.Dart will face American Peyton Stearns in the first round.The smell of cannabis has become a recurring talking point at Flushing Meadows, with players from outside Britain raising similar concerns in previous editions.In 2022, Australian doubles player Nick Kyrgios complained that a spectator smoking courtside was affecting his asthma, prompting the umpire to ask fans to refrain from smoking.A year later, Greece's Maria Sakkari pointed out the smell to the umpire during a match. She later clarified that it was not an excuse for her defeat.Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev have also previously noticed the smell around the tournament.The United States Tennis Association, which organises the US Open, has acknowledged the difficulty of dealing with activity taking place beyond the tournament grounds.“While we can't control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this,” the USTA said in a statement.The organisation has said it works with local police and the parks department to address smoking around the boundary of the site.With the 2026 US Open getting under way on Sunday, the cannabis smell is likely to remain a background issue at a tournament already filled with major storylines. Alcaraz will return to action, Sinner will be absent, Djokovic will chase another historic title, Eala will look to make the most of strong local support and Sabalenka will aim to regain her winning form.Boulter will open against American wildcard Carol Young Suh Lee, while Jones and Dart begin their campaigns against Linette and Stearns respectively.
Article Summary: Cannabis is legal for adults aged 21 and over in New York, although smoking is not permitted on the grounds of the tennis center. The venue sits beside Corona Park, and the smell can carry across to some practice and outside courts. British players Katie Boulter, Fran Jones and Harriet Dart have all noticed the smell around the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.

Article Title: 'Has to be a joke': Pakistan-born cricketer hits out at PCB amid Imran Khan row
Article Text:
Imran Khan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Australia cricketer Usman Khawaja has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) after it complained to a British broadcaster for an interview with the sons of former Pakistan Prime Minister and World Cup-winning captain Imran Khan.Khawaja, who was born in Islamabad, reacted after reports claimed the Pakistan team had threatened to boycott the second Test against England if the broadcaster aired the interview with Imran Khan's sons, Sulaiman and Kasim.The interview was eventually broadcasted, although later than originally scheduled, and Pakistan returned to the field.The PCB lodged a complaint with Sky Sports over the broadcast. Khawaja responded to a social media post about the complaint, writing: “This has got to be a joke".Imran Khan, 73, has been in jail in Rawalpindi since 2023 after being convicted on corruption charges. Earlier this week, he underwent a medical examination in Islamabad before being taken back to prison.His sons have raised concerns about his safety and alleged that attempts are being made on his life.Khawaja's former Australia teammate Pat Cummins also spoke about the issue, saying Imran's family should be allowed access to him.Cummins backed former Australia captain Greg Chappell and 20 other former international captains who recently appealed to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to ensure proper medical care and humane treatment for Imran.Cummins said he hopes the court-ordered medical assessment is completed and that family visits continue. He also called for Imran to be treated with dignity in a post on X while sharing a video of Chappell expressing concern over the former Pakistan captain's health.Cummins became one of the first active international cricketers to publicly support calls for Imran's medical care after 21 former captains, including India's Sunil Gavaskar, signed the letter to the Pakistan Prime Minister.Before entering politics, Imran Khan led Pakistan to its first and only ODI World Cup title in 1992 and remains one of the country's most recognised cricket figures.
Article Summary: Khawaja criticises Pakistan Cricket Board for complaining to Sky Sports. Sky Sports broadcast an interview with Imran Khan's sons Sulaiman and Kasim. Pakistan team reportedly threatened to boycott the second Test against England if the interview was aired. The interview was eventually broadcasted, although later than originally scheduled.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
